question_text: Which frequency range (FR1) is defined for 5G NR in the standard?
options: 410 MHz to 7.125 GHz, covering the lower and mid-band frequencies.
24 GHz to 52 GHz, which provides high bandwidth over shorter distances.
1 GHz to 2.6 GHz, typically reserved for older 3G and 4G deployments.
26 GHz to 66 GHz, commonly referred to as the mmWave frequency band.
correct_answer: 410 MHz to 7.125 GHz, covering the lower and mid-band frequencies.

question_text: In a 5G Radio Access Network, what is the primary role of the Packet Data Convergence Protocol (PDCP)?
options: It implements baseband and RF processing such as OFDM and MIMO algorithms.
It manages the physical radio resources and maps logical channels to physical ones.
It configures coarse-grained, policy-related aspects of the network pipeline.
It compresses IP headers and provides ciphering and integrity protection.
correct_answer: It compresses IP headers and provides ciphering and integrity protection.

question_text: How does a regenerative (OBP) satellite repeater differ from a transparent (bent-pipe) repeater?
options: It directly amplifies and frequency-shifts the received RF signal without decoding it.
It requires large terrestrial base stations to handle the error-correction processing.
It demodulates the uplink signal into baseband data before remodulating it for downlink.
It acts as a simple relay station that forwards incoming signals including the noise.
correct_answer: It demodulates the uplink signal into baseband data before remodulating it for downlink.

question_text: Which physical signal in 5G NR is used to track phase noise in both uplink and downlink?
options: Channel-state information reference signal (CSI-RS), applied for MIMO rank selection.
Phase-tracking reference signals (PT-RS), sent as a low-density pilot sequence.
Sounding reference signal (SRS), utilized to estimate uplink channel state.
Primary synchronization signal (PSS), used to initially identify the network.
correct_answer: Phase-tracking reference signals (PT-RS), sent as a low-density pilot sequence.

question_text: According to the 5G NR PHY frame structure, how many subframes make up a single 10ms radio frame?
options: A variable number of subframes that scales dynamically based on the subcarrier spacing.
Exactly 10 subframes, each having a fixed duration of 1ms regardless of numerology.
Exactly 14 subframes, corresponding to the number of OFDM symbols in a standard slot.
Exactly 12 subframes, matching the number of consecutive subcarriers in a resource block.
correct_answer: Exactly 10 subframes, each having a fixed duration of 1ms regardless of numerology.

question_text: What characterizes an Earth-moving beam in a Non-Terrestrial Network (NTN)?
options: The beam illuminates different geographic areas on Earth as the satellite moves in its orbit.
The beam relies on terrestrial cell towers to mechanically track user equipment.
The beam covers a fixed region continuously because the satellite is geostationary in this specific network context.
The beam is dynamically steered to remain focused on the exact same location.
correct_answer: The beam illuminates different geographic areas on Earth as the satellite moves in its orbit.

question_text: Which NTN platform operates at altitudes between 8 and 50 km and appears stationary to a fixed observer?
options: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites, completing an orbit roughly every 90 minutes.
Geosynchronous Earth Orbit (GEO) satellites, stationed at approximately 35,786 km.
Medium Earth Orbit (MEO) satellites, often used for global navigation satellite systems.
High-Altitude Platform Stations (HAPS), typically utilizing Earth-fixed beams for coverage.
correct_answer: High-Altitude Platform Stations (HAPS), typically utilizing Earth-fixed beams for coverage.

question_text: Why do terrestrial networks struggle to provide complete global coverage?
options: Fiber optic cables inherently experience too much latency for continuous communication.
The 3GPP standard restricts terrestrial networks from transmitting over large distances.
Deploying infrastructure in sparse or rugged areas is often economically unfeasible and challenging.
Terrestrial base stations require line-of-sight to orbiting satellites to function properly within typical communication frameworks.
correct_answer: Deploying infrastructure in sparse or rugged areas is often economically unfeasible and challenging.

question_text: In the context of 5G Non-Terrestrial Networks, what is service continuity?
options: Providing a large geographic area with the same broadcast content simultaneously.
Ensuring that terrestrial cell towers can handle massive congestion during big events.
Maintaining uninterrupted wireless coverage when users move out of terrestrial cell range.
Replacing all existing ground infrastructure with a dense constellation of LEO satellites.
correct_answer: Maintaining uninterrupted wireless coverage when users move out of terrestrial cell range.

question_text: What is the function of the Physical Broadcast Channel (PBCH) in the 5G downlink?
options: It provides uplink channel estimation for the base station to adjust transmission power.
It configures the coarse-grained scheduling prioritization policies in the control plane.
It transports user data packets directly from the core network to the physical layer.
It carries essential system information required for the user equipment to access the network.
correct_answer: It carries essential system information required for the user equipment to access the network.

question_text: What does a 5G resource block (RB) consist of in the frequency and time domains?
options: It consists of 12 subcarriers in frequency and typically 14 OFDM symbols in time.
It consists of 14 subcarriers in frequency and exactly 12 OFDM symbols in time.
It consists of 15 subcarriers in frequency and exactly 1 millisecond of transmission time.
It consists of 10 subcarriers in frequency and a variable number of symbols depending on speed.
correct_answer: It consists of 12 subcarriers in frequency and typically 14 OFDM symbols in time.

question_text: How do LEO satellites compare to GEO satellites in terms of propagation delay?
options: LEO satellites experience delays around 600 ms because they utilize complex regenerative processing.
LEO satellites exhibit significantly larger delays because their signals should bounce between satellites.
LEO and GEO satellites have nearly identical propagation delays since radio waves travel at light speed.
LEO satellites have much smaller delays (1 to 5 ms) due to their proximity to the Earth.
correct_answer: LEO satellites have much smaller delays (1 to 5 ms) due to their proximity to the Earth.

question_text: What defines a quasi-Earth-fixed beam in satellite communications?
options: The beam covers a specific area for a period, then steers to another area as the satellite moves.
The beam provides coverage chiefly to airborne platforms rather than terrestrial user equipment.
The beam maintains a static position over the Earth because the satellite itself is geostationary.
The beam constantly sweeps across the Earth's surface without lingering on any specific region.
correct_answer: The beam covers a specific area for a period, then steers to another area as the satellite moves.

question_text: Which of the following is a function of the Service Data Adaptation Protocol (SDAP) in the 5G protocol stack?
options: It handles physical channel error correction coding, such as polar coding and LDPC coding.
It transparently forwards baseband radio frames without inspecting the network layer headers.
It implements baseband OFDM processing to increase the spectral efficiency of the transmission.
It assigns Quality of Service (QoS) Flow IDs and maps flows to underlying radio resources.
correct_answer: It assigns Quality of Service (QoS) Flow IDs and maps flows to underlying radio resources.

question_text: What is the primary motivation for integrating NTN with Terrestrial Networks in the 6G vision?
options: To achieve ubiquitous global connectivity by complementing ground-based infrastructure.
To replace aging terrestrial fiber optic cables with completely wireless satellite links.
To increase the bandwidth of terrestrial small cells operating in dense urban environments.
To ensure that older 3G and 4G devices can maintain service without hardware upgrades.
correct_answer: To achieve ubiquitous global connectivity by complementing ground-based infrastructure.

question_text: Which NTN use case refers to broadcasting the same content to a large geographic area efficiently?
options: Service reliability, which establishes redundant communication paths during natural disasters.
Service continuity, which aims to keep mobile users connected as they cross network boundaries.
Service scalability, which optimizes network performance by using large satellite beams.
Service ubiquity, which focuses on providing coverage to unserved and rugged rural locations.
correct_answer: Service scalability, which optimizes network performance by using large satellite beams.

question_text: What is the typical altitude range for Medium Earth Orbit (MEO) satellites?
options: Between 8 and 50 km, typically utilized by stratospheric balloons and solar-powered drones.
Exactly 35,786 km, where the orbital period perfectly matches the Earth's rotational speed.
Between 300 and 1,500 km, allowing for extremely low propagation delay for internet services.
Between 7,000 and 25,000 km, balancing wide coverage with moderate latency.
correct_answer: Between 7,000 and 25,000 km, balancing wide coverage with moderate latency.

question_text: In a satellite communications payload, what role does the Low Noise Amplifier (LNA) play?
options: It provides the massive power required to transmit the carrier signal back to the Earth station.
It shifts the frequency of the carrier signal to prepare it for transmission on the downlink.
It demodulates the radio frequency signal to extract the underlying digital baseband data stream.
It boosts the weak received uplink signal while introducing minimal internal noise.
correct_answer: It boosts the weak received uplink signal while introducing minimal internal noise.

question_text: What is the significance of the Radio Resource Control (RRC) protocol in 5G NR?
options: It operates in the control plane to manage coarse-grained network policies and mobility.
It processes user plane packets to ensure data flows smoothly between the device and application.
It compresses IP headers to reduce the overall payload size over the wireless communication link.
It directly converts digital data streams into analog radio frequencies for the physical antennas.
correct_answer: It operates in the control plane to manage coarse-grained network policies and mobility.

question_text: How does Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) handle subcarrier interference?
options: The subcarriers are separated by wide guard bands that prevent the frequencies from overlapping.
The subcarriers use completely different polarization states to maintain signal independence.
The subcarriers are mathematically orthogonal, so crosstalk cancels out at the center frequency.
The subcarriers are transmitted in distinct time slots to avoid colliding in the frequency domain.
correct_answer: The subcarriers are mathematically orthogonal, so crosstalk cancels out at the center frequency.

question_text: Which satellite subsystem is responsible for maintaining the spacecraft's orientation in orbit?
options: The Electrical Power Subsystem (EPS), which supplies energy to the communications payload.
The Attitude and Orbit Control System (AOCS), which stabilizes the platform.
The Thermal Control Subsystem, which prevents the satellite components from overheating.
The Telemetry, Tracking, and Command (TTC&M) system, which relays health data to the ground.
correct_answer: The Attitude and Orbit Control System (AOCS), which stabilizes the platform.

question_text: What characterizes the physical layer uplink channel PRACH in a 5G network?
options: It transmits acknowledgment signals indicating successful reception of downlink data packets.
It carries the bulk of the user data traffic from the mobile device to the base station.
It handles the initial access procedure when a user device attempts to connect to the network.
It broadcasts crucial system information to all mobile devices within the cell's coverage area.
correct_answer: It handles the initial access procedure when a user device attempts to connect to the network.

question_text: Why are GEO satellites considered disadvantageous for certain real-time applications?
options: Their small beam footprints necessitate thousands of satellites to provide continuous coverage.
Their extreme distance from Earth introduces roughly 600ms of round-trip propagation delay.
Their proximity to the atmosphere causes them to experience severe drag and frequent orbit corrections.
Their rapid movement relative to the Earth requires complex tracking antennas on the ground.
correct_answer: Their extreme distance from Earth introduces roughly 600ms of round-trip propagation delay.

question_text: What is the main function of the feeder link in a satellite communication network?
options: It provides the communication path between the satellite and an Earth ground gateway.
It relays data directly from the terrestrial core network to a local base station.
It connects the end-user's mobile device directly to the orbiting satellite.
It establishes a direct optical or radio connection between two artificial satellites.
correct_answer: It provides the communication path between the satellite and an Earth ground gateway.

question_text: How does 5G NR utilize orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) in its physical layer?
options: It uses extensive guard bands between subcarriers to prevent signal overlap.
It divides the channel into multiple narrow subcarriers without guard bands, minimizing interference.
It relies solely on time division multiplexing to separate user signals completely.
It allocates single wideband channels to each user to maximize individual throughput within typical communication frameworks.
correct_answer: It divides the channel into multiple narrow subcarriers without guard bands, minimizing interference.

question_text: What characterizes the physical downlink shared channel (PDSCH) in a 5G network?
options: It is used primarily to broadcast crucial system information across the entire cell.
It carries the primary user data and signaling messages from the base station to devices.
It transmits acknowledgment messages for successfully received uplink data packets.
It manages uplink random access requests initiated by the mobile user equipment.
correct_answer: It carries the primary user data and signaling messages from the base station to devices.

question_text: What role does the MAC protocol play in the 5G NR protocol stack?
options: It provides security mechanisms such as ciphering and integrity protection for data.
It supports multiplexing, prioritization, and scheduling of data across the radio interface.
It maps quality of service flows onto the underlying radio resources for the user plane.
It implements baseband OFDM processing and handles the physical MIMO algorithms.
correct_answer: It supports multiplexing, prioritization, and scheduling of data across the radio interface.

question_text: In the context of the 5G Service-Based Architecture, what is a Network Function (NF)?
options: A terrestrial transport link that connects the core network directly to the public internet.
An entity that provides specific network services through standardized service-based interfaces.
A physical hardware appliance dedicated to converting digital signals into radio waves.
A specialized satellite payload component designed to process baseband data in orbit.
correct_answer: An entity that provides specific network services through standardized service-based interfaces.

question_text: How is a subframe defined in the time domain of the 5G NR physical layer?
options: It is a fixed 1ms time unit that contains a variable number of slots based on numerology.
It is a 10ms structure that encapsulates all resource blocks transmitted in a single cycle.
It is a scheduling unit that consistently contains exactly 14 OFDM symbols in all modes.
It is a flexible time unit whose duration changes depending on the subcarrier spacing.
correct_answer: It is a fixed 1ms time unit that contains a variable number of slots based on numerology.

question_text: What defines legacy satellite communication before the advent of NTN convergence?
options: It was primarily based on short-range Bluetooth and Wi-Fi transmission systems.
It required proprietary hardware and isolated networks for specific missions.
It relied on standardized 3GPP protocols integrated into mainstream mobile networks.
It utilized densely deployed low-power base stations across urban environments.
correct_answer: It required proprietary hardware and isolated networks for specific missions.

question_text: In the context of telecom ecosystems, what is the significance of 3GPP Release 17 for NTN?
options: It mandated the exclusive use of high-altitude platform stations over LEO satellites.
It removed the requirement for satellites to utilize Earth-fixed tracking beams.
It introduced the first standardized 5G NR enhancements specifically for satellite access.
It defined the baseline 4G LTE air interface for terrestrial mobile broadbands.
correct_answer: It introduced the first standardized 5G NR enhancements specifically for satellite access.

question_text: How does NTN aim to solve the coverage limitation of terrestrial networks?
options: By increasing the transmit power of existing ground-based cell towers significantly.
By laying extensive subsea fiber optic cables to connect remote island communities.
By deploying micro-cells on every residential building in sparsely populated areas.
By placing radio network equipment on airborne or spaceborne vehicles for wide coverage.
correct_answer: By placing radio network equipment on airborne or spaceborne vehicles for wide coverage.

question_text: What is an example of an airborne NTN platform as discussed in the course?
options: A terrestrial base station equipped with high-gain directional tracking antennas.
A geostationary earth orbit (GEO) satellite positioned at 35,786 km altitude.
A low earth orbit (LEO) satellite constellation passing quickly overhead.
A high-altitude platform station (HAPS) or an unmanned aerial vehicle (drone).
correct_answer: A high-altitude platform station (HAPS) or an unmanned aerial vehicle (drone).

question_text: According to the NTN use case categories, what does service scalability enable?
options: The efficient broadcasting or multicasting of content over a very large geographic area.
The seamless handover of user equipment between multiple terrestrial cell towers.
The ability to increase physical bandwidth on a single localized point-to-point link.
The deployment of thousands of small cells to handle high-density urban traffic.
correct_answer: The efficient broadcasting or multicasting of content over a very large geographic area.

question_text: Which scenario best illustrates the 'service continuity' use case of an NTN?
options: A smart home thermostat communicating with a local Wi-Fi router during a blackout.
A user downloading a massive software update overnight in a dense urban environment.
A passenger maintaining a data connection while flying over an ocean out of cell range.
A localized network providing ultra-low latency for industrial robotic automation.
correct_answer: A passenger maintaining a data connection while flying over an ocean out of cell range.

question_text: In satellite orbit mechanics, what happens as a satellite's altitude decreases?
options: Its orbital period increases because it should travel faster to counteract gravity.
Its field of view over the Earth's surface expands to cover a larger area.
Its orbital speed increases and its orbital period reduces significantly.
Its signal propagation delay increases due to atmospheric friction effects.
correct_answer: Its orbital speed increases and its orbital period reduces significantly.

question_text: Why are LEO constellations like Starlink able to achieve low round-trip latency?
options: They bypass the 5G core network mostly and route data directly between users.
Their altitude is roughly 550 kilometers, greatly reducing the signal travel distance.
They use extremely high-power transmitters that accelerate radio wave propagation.
They operate chiefly using optical inter-satellite links instead of radio frequencies.
correct_answer: Their altitude is roughly 550 kilometers, greatly reducing the signal travel distance.

question_text: What is a significant disadvantage of using GEO satellites for real-time communication?
options: The satellite should frequently fire its thrusters to maintain its altitude against drag.
The immense distance to the satellite results in approximately 600ms of latency.
The Earth's atmosphere blocks the specific frequency bands allocated to GEO orbits.
The satellite moves too quickly across the sky, requiring complex tracking antennas.
correct_answer: The immense distance to the satellite results in approximately 600ms of latency.

question_text: How many MEO satellites are typically required to provide full global coverage?
options: MEO satellites cannot provide global coverage due to their altitude.
Exactly one satellite positioned strategically over the equator.
Around 6 satellites, properly spaced in their orbits.
Hundreds to thousands of satellites in a dense constellation.
correct_answer: Around 6 satellites, properly spaced in their orbits.

question_text: What characterizes an Earth-fixed beam used by GEO satellites and HAPS?
options: It covers a specific, stationary region on the Earth's surface at all times.
It dynamically steers to track moving airplanes and maritime vessels.
It moves continuously across the planet's surface as the platform orbits.
It provides narrow, localized coverage that changes shape based on traffic.
correct_answer: It covers a specific, stationary region on the Earth's surface at all times.

question_text: Which beam type covers an area for a period and then steers to a new area as the satellite moves?
options: A terrestrial micro-beam.
A quasi-Earth-fixed beam.
An Earth-fixed beam.
An Earth-moving beam.
correct_answer: A quasi-Earth-fixed beam.

question_text: What is the primary function of the 'bus' in a satellite space segment?
options: It routes baseband data packets between different communication transponders.
It provides essential support subsystems like power, thermal control, and propulsion.
It acts as the primary transmitting antenna for downlink communication links.
It demodulates and decodes the radio frequency signals received from the ground.
correct_answer: It provides essential support subsystems like power, thermal control, and propulsion.

question_text: In a satellite communication payload, what is the role of a bent-pipe repeater?
options: It simply amplifies and frequency-translates the received signal before retransmitting.
It actively tracks user equipment on the ground to dynamically adjust beam steering.
It fully demodulates the signal to baseband, corrects errors, and remodulates it.
It converts incoming radio frequency signals into optical signals for inter-satellite links.
correct_answer: It simply amplifies and frequency-translates the received signal before retransmitting.

question_text: What is a key advantage of a regenerative (on-board processing) satellite repeater?
options: It decodes and corrects errors in the baseband signal, retransmitting a clean copy.
It operates across all possible frequency bands without requiring a frequency mixer.
It reflects the incoming signal perfectly without utilizing any internal power sources.
It is much simpler and cheaper to manufacture than a standard bent-pipe repeater.
correct_answer: It decodes and corrects errors in the baseband signal, retransmitting a clean copy.

question_text: Which satellite link connects the satellite to an Earth ground gateway?
options: The service link.
The feeder link.
The terrestrial backhaul link.
The inter-satellite link.
correct_answer: The feeder link.

question_text: In 5G NR, what does the Physical Downlink Control Channel (PDCCH) carry?
options: Scheduling assignments and control information necessary for decoding data.
Synchronization signals used by the device to initially acquire the network.
The primary application data payload directed to the mobile user equipment.
Channel state information feedback sent from the user device to the base station.

question_text: What is the purpose of the Tracking Reference Signal (TRS) in 5G NR?

It assists the user equipment with time and frequency tracking and Doppler estimation.
It provides ciphering keys for securing the user plane data transmission pipeline.
It broadcasts the unique identifier of the cell to all devices within its coverage area.
correct_answer: It assists the user equipment with time and frequency tracking and Doppler estimation.

question_text: Which 5G NR protocol layer handles multiplexing, scheduling, and HARQ retransmissions?
options: The Medium Access Control (MAC) layer.
The Service Data Adaptation Protocol (SDAP) layer.
The Packet Data Convergence Protocol (PDCP) layer.
The Radio Resource Control (RRC) layer.

question_text: What is the primary responsibility of the Radio Resource Control (RRC) protocol?

It performs baseband OFDM processing and multiple-input multiple-output encoding.
It maps application quality of service flows onto the underlying radio resources.

It serves as the main repository for user subscription data and authentication keys.
It provides physical layer error correction and digital-to-analog signal conversion.

question_text: How does 5G NR organize its physical channel resources in the time domain?
options: Into 10ms radio frames, which are divided into 1ms subframes containing slots.
Into 14ms transmission time intervals that correspond to the number of subcarriers.
Into infinitely variable streams without strict frame boundaries to reduce latency.
Into fixed 1ms frames that scale dynamically based on the number of active users.
correct_answer: Into 10ms radio frames, which are divided into 1ms subframes containing slots.

question_text: What is the primary characteristic of Frequency Range 2 (FR2) in 5G?
options: It serves as the primary control plane link between base stations and the core network.
It utilizes low-band frequencies below 1 GHz to provide expansive rural coverage.
It operates in the mmWave bands from 24 to 52 GHz, offering high speeds at short distances.
It is dedicated mostly to non-terrestrial networks operating in geostationary orbit.
correct_answer: It operates in the mmWave bands from 24 to 52 GHz, offering high speeds at short distances.

question_text: Which uplink physical channel is used by a device to initiate connection to a 5G network?
options: The Physical Random-Access Channel (PRACH).
The Physical Uplink Shared Channel (PUSCH).
The Physical Broadcast Channel (PBCH).
The Physical Uplink Control Channel (PUCCH).

question_text: What is the main function of the Sounding Reference Signal (SRS)?

It alerts the user equipment of an incoming paging message from the core network.
It allows the base station to estimate the uplink channel state for scheduling.
